claim: AC #1: A lowercase snake_case column identifier shows its humanized label as the header in the interactive table widget (e.g. customer_id -> "Customer ID").
AC #2: The Markdown table that non-Apps clients receive shows the same humanized header, so widget and Markdown fallback match for every column.
AC #3: A chart axis whose field is a lowercase snake_case identifier and whose label was not set by the LLM shows the humanized field as its axis title (e.g. total_amount_usd -> "Total Amount USD").
AC #4: Every name that is not a lowercase snake_case identifier (uppercase letter, space, or other char) is displayed unchanged, and a chart axis label the LLM set is preserved exactly.
AC #5: Humanizing splits on underscores, capitalizes first letter of each word, and fully upper-cases any word in a known acronym set (at minimum id, url, api, db, sql, ip, uuid).
AC #6: The raw column names carried in the table payload are unchanged, so typed column sort and column_types lookup keep matching on original names.
AC #7: Chart legend entries and series names are unchanged.
AC #8: The humanizer is idempotent: passing an already-humanized label returns it unchanged.

The docstring asserts a humanized label EITHER contains a space or an uppercase letter (passthrough branch returns it as-is) OR maps to itself under the transform (e.g. a pure-digit word like 2024), so feeding it back returns it unchanged. Two-branch exhaustive disjunction (fixed at HEAD; iter-1 carried the universal-claim wording that FAILed).
source_excerpt: That passthrough makes the transform idempotent: a humanized label either contains a space or an uppercase letter (so the passthrough branch returns it as-is) or maps to itself under the transform (e.g. a pure-digit word like ``2024``), so feeding it back returns it unchanged.

claim: The regex comment asserts anything with an uppercase letter, space, punctuation, non-ASCII char, or _id/id_/a__b degenerate underscore FAILS to match and is returned verbatim.
source_excerpt: Anything else (an uppercase letter, a space, punctuation, a non-ASCII character, `_id`, `id_`, `a__b`) fails to match and is returned verbatim.

claim: _default_axis_label assumes the chart spec's x/y are dicts with 'field' and 'label' keys; a non-dict axis or non-string/empty field is returned unchanged.
The HTML widget reads block.column_labels as a parallel array and indexes state.labels[i] against state.columns[i]; assumes labels array aligns positionally with columns.
test_chart_payload.py _spec_axis helper builds a chart spec inline with keys matching what _compute_chart_payload / make_chart consume.
The binary-search truncation loop now re-sets payload['row_count']=mid and payload['truncated']=total-mid before measuring, so the measured serialized length reflects the actual carried values.
_display_labels falls back to raw columns when column_labels is absent or its length differs from columns, so pre-existing/producer payloads without the field still render.
test_format.py asserts the table block exactly equals a dict that now includes 'column_labels': ['Name', 'Age'] between 'columns' and 'rows'.
